rationale: itnet-claude-agentic: pretrain_epochs=120, pretrain_lr=0.001, itnet_k=1, itnet_alpha=0.1, unet_c=16, finetune_epochs=0, finetune_lr=0.0001, train_n=400, val_n=200, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42, rationale=iter-3 (breast ItNet v1, search-20260703-01). SIX-BOX: (1) PRIOR NUMBERS: iter-1 (k=5, ep=20) ssim 0.8237 hr 0.0000 elapsed 212s; iter-2 (k=5, ep=120) ssim 0.7114 hr 0.0000 elapsed 1184s. CRITICAL SIGNAL: 6x MORE pretraining made ssim DROP 0.8237->0.7114 -> the denoiser is NOT under-trained; MORE denoising quality gets DESTROYED downstream. (2) FAILURE MODE: the FIXED analytic k=5 DC unroll re-injects sparse-view streaks. Mechanism: x <- x_denoised - alpha*FBP(R*x_denoised - g); on a 128-view sparse system FBP(residual) is itself a streaky sparse-view recon, so each of the 5 fixed (untrained) DC steps drags the clean denoised image back toward the streaky FBP, raising RMSE above baseline. A cleaner x_denoised (iter-2) is corrupted MORE by 5 steps -> ssim fell. On Mayo the v1 CHAMPION used k=1 for exactly this reason. (3) ONE KNOB: itnet_k 5 -> 1 (all else identical to iter-2: ep=120, alpha=0.1, unet_c=16, lr=1e-3, train_n=400, val_n=200). (4) HYPOTHESIS: if I cut the fixed DC unroll to a single step (k=1), I expect hr to clear 0 and ssim to jump back above iter-1, because the dominant damage is the repeated streak re-injection; one mild DC step barely perturbs the clean denoiser output. FALSIFIER: if hr is still 0 at k=1, the DC step itself (any alpha>0) is net-harmful on sparse breast -> iter-4 drops alpha toward 0 (or k stays 1 with alpha lowered). (5) BUDGET: k=1 is CHEAPER than k=5 (1 forward+FBP per val slice instead of 5); iter-2 at k=5/ep=120 was 1184s, so k=1/ep=120 predicts well under 1000s < 1200s budget. (6) Loop continues; iter-4 dispatched on landing via numeric-headroom gate.
